newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - Bearish build in APIs shows delayed reaction.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Bearish build in APIs shows delayed reaction.

text.p: The sharp build up in gasoline, distillate and crude stocks last week is a delayed reaction to recent high prices, analysts said after Tuesday's American Petroleum Institute (API) weekly inventory report.
"Those are some big numbers," said Raoul le Blanc, an analyst at Energy Security Analysis in Washington, of the report.

Gasoline stocks rose particularly sharply, adding nearly six million barrels to stand at almost 195 million barrels last week. Distillates -- heating oil and diesel -- rose more than two million barrels to 122 million barrels.

Even crude stocks, which rose a modest 324,000 barrels nationally, were up much more when the 2.2 million barrel decline in the west coast (PADD V) area, which is considered an erratic market, is stripped out. The key Gulf of Mexico (PADD III) refining area stocks rose just over three million barrels to 151 million barrels, 3.6 million barrels higher than the same time last year last year.
A 1.5 million rise in imports last week was a big factor in the build up.

Analysts said that the movement in stocks is a delayed reaction to high prices seen in October and November. Though demand has recently tailed off as stocks built up and weather moderated, the high levels of production are likely to continue for a while yet.
"We know that many refiners were able to lock in the excellent spreads on offer over the last month or so and they are going to continue to crank out production," said le Blanc.

A month or so ago refiners could lock in through the futures market through to January or so profitable prices for refined products which have rarely been seen in recent years. Having locked in those prices they are able to continue producing at apparently loss-making cash market levels.
Cash market traders said they expect the latest report to add to recent downward pressure on prices.
"The gasoline build is huge. The No. 2 (heating oil) build is huge. These aren't good numbers -- the market is going to move lower," one Gulf Coast products trader said.
"The APIs should bury the gasoline market," one Gulf gasoline trader said, pointing to the 6.0 million barrel build in total U.S. gasoline stocks over the prior week.
"It's been nothing but sellers for the last four days and now this! It won't be pretty," he said.
The trader said the gasoline market has enjoyed a sizzling rally since November, thanks in great part to strong heating oil prices that have hovered 20 cents a gallon over this time last year.

But the latest APIs have removed some of that heating oil support, he said, noting a 1.0 million barrel build in total stocks for the week -- including a 665,000 barrel gain in the key East Coast market.

The region remains 11.9 million barrels, or 29 percent, shy of last year's heating oil inventories. But that compares with shortfalls of 40 percent a few months ago and warm weather forecasts for the next week have crimped demand, traders said.
